findings.claim: WithRequestID reflects the caller-supplied X-Request-ID value into the response header without any validation or length bound. A caller can send an unbounded value (here 64 KiB, up to the ~1 MB header limit) and the server echoes every byte back on each response, which also lets the client dictate the id used for log correlation (spoofed/duplicated ids, response amplification). Only generated ids are bounded; the echo path is not.

proof.Reason: the test did not build on the fixed tree, and a build error is not a pass

findings.claim: The caller's X-Request-ID is copied verbatim into the response header with no sanitisation. A value containing CR/LF is stored unmodified in the response header map, so the middleware emits a header value carrying injected header content (test shows the value coming out as abc CRLF Set-Cookie: ...). With the standard net/http server this corrupts the response header/breaks the response, and any downstream writer that emits the header raw (proxies, log shippers) can be made to inject extra headers.

proof.Reason: the test did not build on the fixed tree, and a build error is not a pass
